answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a quartz-hard bond that is slashed when duplicate identities are proven. An attacker facing an ocean of honest agents must fund each fake identity separately, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly while honest work stays cheap. Over a long horizon, slashing plus slow reputation accrual makes faking identities unprofitable: a new identity earns little until it has a history, so spinning up thousands of fresh accounts buys almost no influence.
